title_en: Regulations on the Protection of Layout Designs of Integrated Circuits

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of protecting the exclusive rights in layout-designs of integrated circuits, encouraging innovation in integrated circuit technology, and promoting the development of science and technology.

Article 3 The layout-design created by a Chinese natural person, legal person or other organization shall enjoy the exclusive right in the layout-design in accordance with these Regulations.
The layout-design created by a foreign natural person, legal person or other organization, which is first commercially exploited within the territory of China, shall enjoy the exclusive right in the layout-design in accordance with these Regulations.
The layout-design created by a foreign natural person, legal person or other organization, where the country to which the creator belongs has entered into an agreement on the protection of layout-design with China or is a party to an international treaty on the protection of layout-design to which China is also a party, shall enjoy the exclusive right in the layout-design in accordance with these Regulations.

Article 4 A protected layout-design shall be original, that is, it shall be the result of the creator's own intellectual effort and shall not be among the conventional designs commonly recognized among creators of layout-designs and manufacturers of integrated circuits at the time of its creation.
A protected layout-design that is composed of conventional designs shall, as a whole, satisfy the conditions set out in the preceding paragraph.
Article 5 The protection of layout-design under these Regulations shall not extend to ideas, processing procedures, methods of operation, or mathematical concepts, etc.

Article 6 The intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall be responsible for the administration of matters relating to the exclusive rights in layout-designs in accordance with these Regulations.

Article 8 The exclusive right in a layout-design shall be created upon registration with the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council.
A layout-design that has not been registered shall not be protected under these Regulations.

Article 9 The exclusive right in a layout-design shall belong to the creator of the layout-design, unless otherwise provided in these Regulations.
Where a layout-design is created under the direction of and on the basis of the will of a legal person or other organization, and the legal person or other organization assumes the responsibility for such layout-design, such legal person or other organization shall be deemed the creator.
Where a layout-design is created by a natural person, such natural person shall be the creator.

Article 10 Where a layout-design is created jointly by two or more natural persons, legal persons or other organizations, the ownership of the exclusive right in the layout-design shall be agreed upon by the co-creators; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the exclusive right shall be jointly owned by the co-creators.

Article 11 Where a layout-design is created under commission, the ownership of the exclusive right in the layout-design shall be agreed upon by the commissioning party and the commissioned party; where there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the exclusive right shall be enjoyed by the commissioned party.

Article 12 The term of protection of the exclusive right in a layout-design shall be 10 years, calculated from the date of the filing of an application for registration of the layout-design or from the date of its first commercial exploitation anywhere in the world, whichever is earlier. However, regardless of whether it is registered or commercially exploited, a layout-design shall no longer be protected under these Regulations after the expiration of 15 years from the date of its creation.

Article 13 Where the exclusive right in a layout-design belongs to a natural person, upon the death of that natural person, the exclusive right shall be transferred within the term of protection specified in these Regulations in accordance with the provisions of the Succession Law.
Where the exclusive right in a layout-design belongs to a legal person or other organization, upon the change or termination of that legal person or other organization, the exclusive right shall, within the term of protection specified in these Regulations, be enjoyed by the legal person or other organization that succeeds to its rights and obligations. If there is no legal person or other organization that succeeds to its rights and obligations, such layout-design shall enter into the public domain.

Article 14 The intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall be responsible for the registration of layout-designs and shall accept applications for registration of layout-designs.

Article 15 Where a layout-design for which registration is applied involves State security or major interests and needs to be kept confidential, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 17 Where an application for registration of a layout-design is not filed with the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council within two years from the date of its first commercial exploitation anywhere in the world, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall no longer register it.

Article 18 Where, after preliminary examination of an application for registration of a layout-design, no grounds for refusal are found, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall register it, issue a registration certificate, and announce it.

Article 19 Where an applicant for registration of a layout-design is dissatisfied with the decision of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council to refuse the registration application, the applicant may, within three months from the date of receipt of the notification, request a review by the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council. The intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall, after review, make a decision and notify the applicant for registration of the layout-design. If the applicant for registration of the layout-design is still dissatisfied with the review decision of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council, the applicant may, within three months from the date of receipt of the notification, institute legal proceedings in a People's Court.

Article 20 Where, after a layout-design has been registered, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council finds that the registration does not conform to the provisions of these Regulations, it shall revoke such registration, notify the holder of the layout-design right, and announce such revocation. If the holder of the layout-design right is dissatisfied with the decision of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council to revoke the registration of the layout-design, the holder may, within three months from the date of receipt of the notification, institute legal proceedings in a People's Court.

Article 21 Before the announcement of the registration of a layout-design, staff members of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall have the duty to keep its contents confidential.

Article 22 The holder of the exclusive right in a layout-design may assign the exclusive right or license another person to use the layout-design.
Where the exclusive right in a layout-design is assigned, the parties shall enter into a written contract, register it with the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council, and the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall announce it. The assignment of the exclusive right in a layout-design shall take effect as of the date of registration.
Where a license to use the layout-design is granted to another person, the parties shall enter into a written contract.

Article 24 After a protected layout-design, an integrated circuit incorporating such layout-design, or an article incorporating such an integrated circuit has been placed on the market by the holder of the layout-design right or with the holder's permission, any subsequent commercial exploitation by another person may be carried out without the permission of, and without the payment of remuneration to, the holder of the layout-design right.

Article 25 Where a state of emergency or extraordinary circumstances occurs in the country, or for the purposes of the public interest, or where the People's Court or the supervisory and inspection department for acts of unfair competition has, pursuant to law, determined that the holder of the layout-design right has committed an act of unfair competition and a remedy is required, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council may grant a non-voluntary license to use the layout-design.

Article 26 Where the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council makes a decision to grant a non-voluntary license to use a layout-design, it shall promptly notify the holder of the layout-design right.
The decision to grant a non-voluntary license to use a layout-design shall, based on the reasons for the non-voluntary license, specify the scope and duration of such use. The scope shall be limited to non-commercial use for public purposes, or to the remedy required where the People's Court or the supervisory and inspection department for acts of unfair competition has, pursuant to law, determined that the holder of the layout-design right has committed an act of unfair competition.
When the reasons for the non-voluntary license cease to exist and are unlikely to recur, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council shall, upon the request of the holder of the layout-design right, after examination, make a decision to terminate the non-voluntary license to use the layout-design.

Article 27 A natural person, legal person or other organization that obtains a non-voluntary license to use a layout-design shall not have an exclusive right to use such layout-design and shall have no right to authorize others to use it.

Article 28 A natural person, legal person or other organization that obtains a non-voluntary license to use a layout-design shall pay a reasonable remuneration to the holder of the layout-design right. The amount of such remuneration shall be negotiated by the parties. If the parties fail to reach an agreement, the matter shall be adjudicated by the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council.

Article 29 If the holder of the layout-design right is dissatisfied with the decision of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council regarding the non-voluntary license to use a layout-design, or if the holder of the layout-design right or the natural person, legal person or other organization that has obtained the non-voluntary license is dissatisfied with the adjudication of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council regarding the remuneration for the non-voluntary license, they may, within three months from the date of receipt of the notification, institute legal proceedings in a People's Court.

Article 30 Except as otherwise provided in these Regulations, where any of the following acts is committed without the permission of the holder of the layout-design right, the actor must immediately stop the infringing act and shall bear compensation liability:
(1) Reproducing the protected layout-design as a whole or any original part thereof;
(2) Importing, selling or otherwise providing for commercial purposes a protected layout-design, an integrated circuit incorporating such layout-design, or an article incorporating such an integrated circuit.
The amount of compensation for infringement of the exclusive right in a layout-design shall be the profits gained by the infringer or the losses suffered by the infringed party, including the reasonable expenses incurred by the infringed party for stopping the infringing act.

Article 31 Where any dispute arises from the use of a layout-design without the permission of the holder of the exclusive right in the layout-design, thereby infringing the exclusive right in the layout-design, the parties shall settle such dispute through consultation. If the parties are unwilling to consult or if consultation fails, the holder of the layout-design right or an interested party may institute legal proceedings in a People's Court, or may request the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council to handle the matter. When the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council handles the matter and determines that the infringing act is established, it may order the infringer to immediately stop the infringing act, and may confiscate and destroy the infringing products or articles. If a party is dissatisfied, it may, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the notification of the handling decision, institute legal proceedings in a People's Court in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If the infringer neither institutes legal proceedings nor ceases the infringing act upon the expiration of the time limit, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council may request the People's Court to enforce the decision. Upon the request of a party, the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council may mediate the amount of compensation for infringement of the exclusive right in the layout-design. If mediation fails, the parties may institute legal proceedings in a People's Court in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 32 Where the holder of the layout-design right or an interested party has evidence to prove that another person is committing or is about to commit an act infringing its exclusive right, and that failure to stop such act promptly will cause irreparable damage to its lawful rights and interests, it may, before instituting legal proceedings, apply to a People's Court in accordance with the law for measures to order the cessation of the relevant act and for property preservation.

Article 33 A person who, at the time of obtaining an integrated circuit incorporating a protected layout-design or an article incorporating such an integrated circuit, did not know and had no reasonable grounds to know that such integrated circuit or article contained an unlawfully reproduced layout-design, and commercially exploits it, shall not be deemed to have committed infringement.
After the person referred to in the preceding paragraph receives express notification that the integrated circuit or article contains an unlawfully reproduced layout-design, that person may continue to commercially exploit the existing stock or the goods ordered prior to such notification, but shall pay a reasonable remuneration to the holder of the layout-design right.

Article 34 Where a staff member of the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council, in the administration of layout-designs, neglects duties, abuses powers, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, and such act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the law. If the act does not constitute a crime, administrative sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the law.

Article 35 Fees shall be paid in accordance with the provisions for applying for registration of layout-designs and handling other formalities. The fee standards shall be formulated by the competent pricing department of the State Council and the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council, and shall be announced by the intellectual property administrative department of the State Council.
Article 36 These Regulations shall come into force as of October 1, 2001.
